Mr. P.V. Arul Pazham Nee for R3

judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

V. Bharathidasan, J.:— This Writ Petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the 1st respondent under Sec.78 of H.R. & C.E. Act (hereinafter called as ‘Act’) and also consequential order passed by the 2nd respondent.

2. According to the petitioner, the property in dispute belongs to the 3rd respondent temple, it has been leased out to the petitioners predecessors in the year 1904 for a period of 99 years. Thereafter, the petitioners are in possession and enjoyment of the property. Now, without conducting any enquiry and without giving any opportunity to the petitioners, the 1st respondent has passed an order of eviction and consequently, the 2nd respondent has also issued a notice calling upon the petitioners to vacate the premises. Challenging both the orders, the present Writ Petition has been filed.

3. Mr. J. Lakshminarayanan, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioners are in possession and enjoyment of the property for more than 100 years. Now, the Joint Commissioner/1st respondent, without conducting proper enquiry and without giving opportunity to the petitioners passed an exparte order of eviction. The learned counsel has further submitted that pending Writ Petition, pursuant to the interim order granted by this Court, the petitioners have also deposited a sum of Rs. 6 lakhs. The order has been passed without conducting proper enquiry and without giving opportunity to the petitioner is violation of principles of natural justice, the petitioners have filed this Writ Petition.

4. Mr. M. Maharaja, learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 submitted that earlier, the lease was granted to the petitioner and the same was expired in the year 2003 itself. Thereafter, without paying any rent to the temple, the petitioners are in possession and enjoyment of the property. Hence, the petitioners were treated as encroachers and the proceedings have been initiated against them under Section 18 of the Act. Notices were also served on the petitioners and they have appeared through their counsels, but, they did not file any objections for more than five years. In the above circumstances, the 1st respondent on considering the entire materials on record, had passed an order of eviction, there is no illegality in the order passed by the 1st respondent. That apart, the learned counsel has submitted that it is not an exparte order, against the order passed by the 1st respondent, a revision lies under Sec.21 of the Act, the petitioner cannot maintain the Writ Petition.

5. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners as well as the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 and the learned counsel appearing for 3rd respondent and perused the records carefully.

6. The primordial contention of the petitioners is that the order of eviction has been passed without giving proper opportunity to the petitioners. But, it is seen that notices were issued to the petitioners and they have also represented through their counsels, but they have not filed any objections. In the said circumstances, considering the matter on merits, the 1st respondent Joint Commissioner had passed an order of eviction. Admittedly, against the order passed by the 1st respondent, a revision lies before the Commissioner under Sec. 21 of the Act and a further revision is also provided under Sec. 114 of the Act, before the Government. Without availing all those alternative remedies, the petitioners cannot challenge the impugned order under Art. 226 of Constitution of India. On that ground alone, the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.

7. However, it is always open to the petitioners to file a revision before the appropriate authority. Considering the fact that the petitioners are in possession of the property for long time, the respondents are directed not to take any steps to evict them for a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.

8. With the above observation, the present Writ Petition stands dismissed. No costs. Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
